items.why: viz3d.js registers exactly two providers, bodyparts3d and svg. There is NO procedural provider, so a model built by this task has nothing to plug into and cannot reach a student. This must be built before any scene can move past 'planned'. Build it as a third provider that resolves a structure key to a builder module under viz-training/models/, mirroring how bodyparts3d resolves a key to an STL. Do not change the two existing providers. Do not touch the frozen Smart-Drill engine. Bump the sw.js CACHE version, reading its CURRENT value first — another session moves it.

built_notes: viz3d.js registers 'procedural' beside bodyparts3d and svg. Same adapter contract: resolve(s) and load(T,s) -> {mesh, reason}. The two existing providers are untouched.
Ref shape is a plain string like bodyparts3d's: refs.procedural = "<model>#<part>", optionally "...@<t>". An object {model,part,t} also parses.

Models live under MEDBANK_CONFIG.MODEL_BASE (default ./models3d/) and register window.MB3D_MODELS[id] = {LAYERS, build, FULL}. render-kit.js is loaded once, before any model, because it reads window.THREE at evaluation.

ONE STRUCTURE, ONE MESH: the engine reads m.geometry directly for highlight patches, anchors and bounding boxes, so a Group would break it. The adapter merges every mesh carrying the key into one geometry and drops silhouette shells.

PROVEN, not assumed: all 8 parts of cardiac-looping resolve with correct triangle counts; unknown part -> 'none'; absent ref -> 'none'; missing model file -> 'failed'; t=0 and t=1 give different geometry; rendered through the app's own lighting rig.

A bug this testing caught: the adapter first built with {}, so any layer behind an option flag (the endocardial tube) came back as 'none' — 'the corpus has no model of this' — which was a lie about a model sitting right there. Models now declare FULL and the adapter builds the complete set.
known_gaps: t is per scene or per structure, NOT per view. A scene cannot yet animate through its own stages with an op — that belongs in the op dispatcher, not the adapter.
Procedural models are in their own units; BodyParts3D meshes are anatomical millimetres. A scene must not mix the two providers until something reconciles scale.

findings: 1. THE ATRIUM AND THE SINUS VENOSUS FINISH ENTIRELY ON THE EMBRYO'S LEFT. The build task declared this itself and could not solve it out; it is confirmed, and the BOUNDING BOX makes it worse than the centroid the builder reported. Measured on real mesh vertices at t=1 (+x = LEFT): atrium x spans +0.151 to +2.017 — it NEVER REACHES THE MEDIAN PLANE, let alone straddles it; sinus x spans -0.085 to +1.716, 95.3% of its width on the left. Centroids atrium +1.101, sinus +0.729 (the builder's centreline figures were +1.14 and +0.66). Why it is a teaching error and not a cosmetic one: the common atrium at day 28 straddles the midline, and the sinus venosus is the RIGHT-sided inflow whose right horn becomes the sinus venarum — the smooth posterior wall of the right atrium and the reason SVC and IVC drain where they do. A student who learns this picture puts the systemic venous inflow on the left. Test J (|atrium x| small) and K (|sinus x| small) exist in the builder's own notes and both FAIL.

2. THE ATRIA ARE NOT ABOVE THE VENTRICLES — NEW, AND NOTHING IN THE TEST SET CONSTRAINS IT. At t=1 the atrium spans y -2.714 to -0.514 (height 2.200) and the ventricle spans y -3.100 to -0.563 (height 2.538). THE OVERLAP IS 2.152, WHICH IS 97.8% OF THE ATRIUM'S OWN VERTICAL EXTENT. Centroid separation D = +0.351, i.e. 16% of the atrium's height. Test D asks only 'atrium y - ventricle y > 0' and +0.351 satisfies it, so the model asserts the relation on every build while the picture does not show it. This is the THIRD movement, which is the entire subject of view 5 ('Movement three — the atria climb up behind') and the second line of view 6's three-sentence exam drill ('atria side by side behind and above them'). For contrast the DORSAL half of the same claim is legible and fine: C = -0.80 with only 58% z-overlap. It is specifically the vertical separation that is missing. Note also that in the world frame the atrium and sinus DESCEND between t=0 and t=1 (atrium y -1.060 to -1.548, sinus -2.249 to -2.702) while the venous pole is nailed at y -2.887, so on screen nothing climbs; the relation only improves because the ventricle descends faster.

3. THE VENTRICLE FINISHES ON THE MEDIAN PLANE, NOT TO THE LEFT — TEST I PASSES ON THE SIGN AND THE PICTURE DOES NOT. Ventricle centroid x = +0.070 on a chamber 1.329 wide: FIVE PER CENT of its own width. Round 2 wrote I as 'ventricle centroid x > 0' and the round-2 rework solved to +0.070, which satisfies it exactly and invisibly. View 4 says 'the primitive ventricle moves backwards and to the left'; views 6 and 8 depend on the future left ventricle being visibly left-posterior, because that is what makes view 8's 'the morphological right ventricle on the left' a legible contrast rather than a caption. A student sees a ventricle in the middle. THIS IS THE SAME FAILURE MODE ROUND 2 FOUND TWICE (finding 2, a test that did not test its own `must` string; finding 4, a test that locked in a defect) NOW RECURRING IN A TEST ROUND 2 ITSELF WROTE. See standards_gap_round_3: the fix is a magnitude floor, not another sign test.

4. THE SINUS VENOSUS IS AN OPEN PIPE AT ITS CAUDAL END, AND IT IS VISIBLE IN VIEWS 3 AND 4. sweptShell() closes every segment with ANNULAR END CAPS, and OVERLAP = 0.006 hides the caps at the four internal waists — but the tube has TWO TERMINAL ends with no neighbour to hide behind. gaps[10] records that view 9 was tried from ABOVE and rejected because it 'looks straight down the truncus and shows its open lumen — the one thing RENDER-STANDARD says must never be visible'. The caudal end of the SINUS has exactly the same cap and was never worked around: it is plainly visible from the ANTERIOR camera at stage _b, which is the camera and the stage that views 3 and 4 both use. Wall ring and lit inner surface are unambiguous in _review-2026-09-10-r3-cardiac-looping/crop-sinus-b.png. The veins cross the opening without plugging it. This is the same defect at the other end of the same tube, avoided at one end by choosing a camera and left exposed at the other — the unlisted place. FIX: do not solve it with a camera. Either carry the sinus caudally into the vein confluence so the veins close it, or cap the terminal ends with a rounded dome rather than an annulus.

5. THE MEDIAN-PLANE REFERENCE IS 96.5% OCCLUDED IN THE ONLY VIEW THAT USES IT. The midline is a rod of RADIUS 0.030 plus three ventral ticks that reach only z = +1.15, while the heart's ventral surface at t=1 reaches z = +1.684 — so the rod lies BEHIND the ventricle and bulbus from the anterior camera. Measured by differencing view 9's own camera with and without midline:true — midline pixels if nothing occluded it 3,525; midline pixels ACTUALLY VISIBLE 125; that is 0.081% of the subject's 154,711 pixels. The reference was added in round 1 (finding 12) specifically so that 'mirror image about the median plane' would be a visible claim rather than a caption, and view 9 HIGHLIGHTs it at intensity 0.6. It does not survive its own view. FIX: draw the plane as a translucent quad in the median plane, or bring the ticks forward past z = +1.7 and thicken the rod, and re-measure the visible pixel count rather than assuming.

6. VIEWS 3 AND 4 NARRATE TWO SEQUENTIAL MOVEMENTS OVER ONE FROZEN STAGE, SO NEITHER MOVEMENT IS VISIBLE AS A MOVEMENT. Both views draw stage _b (t = 0.65) with an IDENTICAL structure set and an identical camera, differing only in which structure is highlighted. They pass the no-duplicate-frame rule as written, and they are not pixel-identical. But all four Gaussian bends grow together with t, so NO value of t separates movement one from movement two: at t = 0.65 the ventricle has already swung dorsally and left whatever view 3's title says, and by stage _c all three movements are complete. A student told 'the first movement is the one that names the loop' is looking at a picture in which the second and third have already happened. gaps[2] declares the per-structure-t mechanism but not this consequence. FIX, and it does not need the engine: give the four bends STAGGERED ONSETS in t so that the bulboventricular bend leads and the sinoatrial bend follows, then add a stage between _a and _b. Do not fix it by re-pointing _b — that was tried in round 1 and the movements still coincide.

7. STATED POSITIVELY — ROUND 2'S FOUR FINDINGS ARE ALL GENUINELY FIXED, RE-VERIFIED WITHOUT THE BUILDER'S PROVERS. The build task asked for exactly this ('prove-mirror-chirality.mjs is not independent evidence — I wrote both the fix and its prover'), so it was done in a harness written for this review. items.standards_gap: RENDER-STANDARD has rules for winding, normals, colour, hulls and frame fill, and every one of them passed here. (a) DECLARE THE AXES AND PROVE THEM. A model states its axis convention in a machine-readable field, and the check asserts it against the corpus: RIGHT is -x, LEFT is +x, CRANIAL +y, VENTRAL +z, measured from BodyParts3D right/left pairs, not from a comment. 'The inflow end comes to lie behind and above the ventricles' is one line of arithmetic, and it fails.

findings_round_1: 1. THE LOOP BENDS DORSALLY, NOT VENTRALLY. This is the biggest one and it is invisible in the anterior view, which is why it survived the build. Measured in world space at t=1, centroid z (model's own +z = ventral): ventricle 0 -> -1.12, bulbus 0 -> -0.82, atrium 0 -> -0.93. Every segment goes backwards. Confirmed by rendering a lateral view with axis rods drawn in: the whole heart sits on the -z side of the original tube axis (viz-training/_review-2026-09-10/diag-t1-lateral.png). View 3 is TITLED 'Movement one - the bulbus swings ventrally, caudally and to the RIGHT' and its narration says 'swings forwards, downwards and to the right'. Ventral and right are the two halves of the D-loop and only the right half is built. A student who rotates the model learns the convexity points backwards. NOT a sign flip: negating z would send the atrium ventral, which is equally wrong. It is the torsion — PSI0 = 0.26 and TAU = 1.60, the two hand-tuned constants in psi(u,t) — that has to carry the cranial limb ventral and the caudal limb dorsal. RENDER-STANDARD's own rule 'PREFER A SOLVED PARAMETER TO A TUNED ONE' applies: the amplitude is solved by bisection, but the torsion, which decides the examinable relation, is guessed. SHARPENED ON RE-CHECK, and correcting my own overstatement: it is NOT true that all three segments are wrong. Beat 4's narration wants the ventricle DORSAL and beat 5 wants the atrium dorsal and cranial, and both of those the model gets right. The relative order of the two limbs is right too — the bulbus is ventral to the ventricle at t = 1 (z -0.82 vs -1.12). Two things are wrong. The BULBUS moves dorsally from its own start (z 0 -> -0.82) while view 3 says it swings forwards, and the whole loop is displaced backwards, which is what puts the ventricle behind the atrium in finding 2. The target for the rebuild is therefore not 'flip z' but 'separate the limbs in the AP axis about an axis that does not itself travel dorsally'.

2. AT DAY 28 THE ATRIUM IS STILL BELOW THE VENTRICLE, AND IS VENTRAL TO IT. Measured at t=1: atrium y centre -0.68 vs ventricle y centre +0.51, so the inflow end is still caudal; atrium z centre -0.93 vs ventricle -1.12, so the ventricle is the more DORSAL of the two. View 5's narration says 'the inflow end comes to lie behind and above the ventricles instead of below them' and view 6 says the atria 'lie side by side behind and above them'. Both are contradicted by the geometry, and view 5 is a LATERAL view, so the student is looking straight at the contradiction while being told the opposite. This is the relation the whole adult mediastinum hangs on. Same root cause as finding 1. QUANTIFIED ON RE-CHECK: the atrium starts 1.48 units below the ventricle at t = 0 and ends 1.19 below at t = 1. The third movement closes 20% of a gap it is supposed to cross. And the AP relation is inverted at every t, worst in mid-loop: ventricle-minus-atrium z is 0.00 at t = 0, -0.33 at t = 0.4, -0.20 at t = 1, where it needs to be positive throughout.

3. THE DORSAL MESOCARDIUM NEVER BREAKS DOWN — IT JUST FADES. mesoAlpha = 1 below t=0.34 then ramps to 0 by t=0.58, and the sheet is one continuous quad strip at every t. There is no version of it with a central gap. View 2's whole teaching payoff is that gap: 'The middle of the dorsal mesocardium has already given way... The gap it leaves behind is the transverse pericardial sinus, which is why in the adult you can pass a finger behind the aorta and pulmonary trunk and in front of the atria.' Nothing in the model can show that. Worse, view 2 shows meso_a, which is 'cardiac-looping#mesocardium@0' and is LABELLED 'Dorsal mesocardium, still intact' — so the picture asserts intact while the narration says broken. And it is worse again than that: the sheet is a median-plane membrane and view 2 does not rotate, so in the anterior view it is edge-on behind the tube and invisible. View 2 renders PIXEL-IDENTICAL to view 1. FIX: build the mesocardium as two cuffs with a real gap between them once t passes the breakdown threshold, give the scene a meso_b at that t, and rotate view 2 to lateral. I did not rotate view 2 on its own — showing an intact sheet clearly under narration that says it has broken down is a worse error than showing nothing, and rotating without the model change would have shipped exactly that.

4. THE PERICARDIUM CANNOT SHOW THE ONE THING IT IS THERE FOR. It is sized from the bounding box of the heart at that same t (box = Box3().setFromObject(heartOnly), then scaled from sz), so the cavity grows with the tube. View 1's narration - the mechanical premise of the entire scene - is 'it is elongating faster than the pericardial cavity around it'. A cavity scaled to the tube can never show a tube outgrowing it. It is also drawn at opacity 0.022, which is invisible. FIX: size the cavity from the day-21 tube and hold it, or grow it on its own slower schedule, so the crowding is visible; then put it on view 1.

At t = 0.4 the tube is a shallow wave: it has bent, but the bulboventricular limbs have not folded alongside one another and there is no C. The recognisable C-loop — ventricle and bulbus folded with a distinct sulcus between them, atrium still caudal — appears at about t = 0.6. Worse for views 3 and 4 specifically: view 4's narration says 'the two now sit side by side rather than one behind the other', and MEASURED, the ventricle-to-bulbus vector is predominantly cranio-caudal at EVERY t — (0.28, 1.25, 0.20) at t = 0.6 and (0.45, 1.09, 0.30) at t = 1. Separately, the model's header defines t = 0 as day 21 while view 1's narration (and the original view 1) call the straight tube day 23; with t = 1 as day 28 those give day 23.8 and day 25 for the same t = 0.4. I did NOT re-point stage _b to 0.6. 12. VIEW 10 DOES TEACH THAT DEXTROCARDIA MEANS L-LOOP, AND THAT IS WRONG. The answer to the queue's own question is yes. The view shows ventricle_l and bulbus_l alone — two mirrored chambers, no atrium, no outflow, no midline, no thorax — immediately after view 9 has established that exact shape as 'the L-loop'. Dextrocardia is a claim about where the heart sits in the chest and which way the apex points, and a model with no body midline cannot make that claim at all: nothing in the frame says right or left. The narration is careful and the geometry contradicts the sentence in it that matters most clinically — 'isolated dextrocardia, with the abdominal organs in the usual place, carries a high rate of associated defects' is describing dextroversion, a D-LOOPED heart rotated into the right chest. Mirror-image dextrocardia with situs inversus is L-looped; dextroversion is not. Showing only the mirrored loop collapses the distinction the view exists to make. The existing gaps[] entry covers dextroposition but not this. FIX: either give the model a body midline / chest reference so position can be shown, or accept that this beat is not a 3D claim and let it run on the same picture as view 9 with the distinction carried in narration. Do not leave it as a mirrored loop captioned 'dextrocardia'.

items.standards_gap_round_2: RENDER-STANDARD.md would not have caught round 2's finding 1, and its own text is part of why. Section 2.1 makes reversed winding the cardinal sin, so a model author writing a mirror is pushed towards the construction trick precisely BECAUSE it leaves winding untouched — and untouched winding is the signature of a rotation. TWO RULES PROPOSED. (a) A MIRRORED VARIANT MUST BE PROVED TO BE A REFLECTION. Chirality is not implied by any check we currently run: triangle count, outward-normal fraction, negated mean x and untouched winding all pass on a 180-degree rotation, and all four were cited as proof here. The test is one line — the signed volume of four named landmark centroids must be NEGATED, not preserved — and it belongs in the model's acceptance(), asserted on the mirror build, which is the build acceptance() never touches. Add the corollary too: a genuine enantiomer MUST reverse winding, so the emitter flips through quadFlip; if a mirror needed no rendering change at all, it is not a mirror. (b) AN ACCEPTANCE TEST MUST BE TESTED AGAINST ITS OWN PROSE. Test G's must string said transverse and its implementation said hypot(transverse, antero-posterior), so the one arrangement the narration denies was counted as evidence for the arrangement it asserts, and a false claim about t = 0.65 propagated from the test into the build notes and into the scene's gaps[]. A test that grades its own homework in the wrong units is worse than no test: it launders a defect into a proof. Every id in an ACCEPTANCE block needs a negative case — a deliberately wrong input the test must reject — the way validate-scenes negative-tests its new checks.
findings_round_2: 1. CRITICAL — THE `mirror` VARIANT IS A 180-DEGREE ROTATION, NOT A REFLECTION, SO VIEW 8 DOES NOT SHOW AN L-LOOP AND VIEW 9 DOES NOT SHOW MIRROR-IMAGE ANATOMY. Proved three independent ways, none of which needs the source. (a) VERTEX LEVEL: every vertex of the D-loop build, transformed and matched against the mirror build — sinus, atrium, ventricle, bulbus and truncus all match rot-Y-180 (x,y,z -> -x,y,-z) at 100.0% and match a true reflect-X (x -> -x) at 0.0%. (b) CHIRALITY: the signed volume of the sinus-atrium-ventricle-bulbus tetrahedron is 0.0427 in BOTH builds, ratio exactly 1.0000. A mirror image must NEGATE it. The two builds have the same handedness, so no amount of rotating the camera will ever make one look like the enantiomer of the other. (c) PICTURE: with one fixed camera and the poles hidden, the mirror build seen from the front is PIXEL-IDENTICAL (sha1 9a4c71e3c9dc) to the normal D-loop simply turned 180 degrees about its long axis — viz-training/_review-2026-09-10-r2/mirror-is-a-rotation.png, panels 2 and 3. WHY IT SURVIVED: integrate() seeds n = (MIRROR ? -1 : +1, 0, 0) and then derives b = d x n, so BOTH frame vectors flip. Negating n and b together is a rotation about the tangent, not a reflection. The build note calls it 'proven' on triangle count, outward-normal fraction, negated mean x and untouched winding — and a rotation passes every one of those. 'The winding is untouched' is the tell, not the proof: a genuine enantiomer MUST reverse winding. CONSEQUENCES. The mirrored build fails the model's own acceptance A (ventricle z -0.554, i.e. convex DORSALLY), C (+1.319, atrium ventral to ventricle) and E (-0.691, bulbus dorsal to ventricle) — acceptance() only ever runs un-mirrored, so nothing caught it. In view 8 the 'L-loop' renders at 79% of the D-loop's width and 81% of its silhouette area with identical height to the pixel, which is the signature of a Y-rotation, in the one view whose entire purpose is comparing the two. And the transform is not even internally consistent: the veins match a TRUE reflection at 100.0%, and the arches match neither (15.6% / 21.7%), so the tube and its poles disagree about what mirroring means. NOT FIXED HERE, deliberately: the fix is a real reflection (negate x on positions, frames and normals) with the ring emission flipped through K.quadFlip so surfaces stay outward, and that is a change to the sweep emitter — the exact surface RENDER-STANDARD 2.1 says must never be hand-rolled twice. I corrected the model's MIRRORING comment, which asserted the opposite, and left the geometry alone. Views 8 and 9 must not go in front of a student until this is done.

2. ACCEPTANCE TEST G DID NOT TEST WHAT ITS OWN `must` STRING SAID — CORRECTED THIS ROUND. The spec reads 'transverse separation of bulbus and ventricle > their cranio-caudal separation'. The implementation was `G: Math.hypot(dx, dz) - Math.abs(dy)`, which folds the ANTERO-POSTERIOR separation in with the transverse one — so 'one behind the other', the single arrangement view 4's narration explicitly denies, was counted as evidence FOR 'side by side'. That is where the build note's 'crossover at t = 0.58, margin +0.11 at t = 0.65' came from; both numbers are artefacts of the conflation. Changed to `G: Math.abs(dx) - Math.abs(dy)`. It still passes (+0.273 on the centreline measure, +0.169 on mesh centroids), console clean, so no new noise — but see finding 3 for the geometry it was hiding. NOTE FOR THE NEXT BUILD: G as corrected is still weaker than the narration. The narration claims side by side rather than one BEHIND the other, which needs a further test dx > dz. That FAILS at every t, worst at t = 1 (dx 0.305 vs dz 0.691). Add it as test H once the geometry can satisfy it; do not add it before, or every render will warn.

3. VIEW 4's 'SIDE BY SIDE' IS FALSE AT THE t THE VIEW ACTUALLY RENDERS. Stage _b is t = 0.65 and views 3 and 4 both draw it. Measured bulbus-vs-ventricle centroid separation at t = 0.65: transverse 0.319, cranio-caudal 0.675, antero-posterior 0.714. The dominant relation is one BEHIND the other — which is what the narration denies in the same sentence: 'the two now sit side by side rather than one behind the other'. Transverse never exceeds cranio-caudal below t = 0.8, so this is NOT fixable by re-pointing stage _b, and I did not re-point it. Bounding-box x-overlap is 1.05 units on chambers about 1.56 wide at t = 1, so they overlap in the transverse axis almost completely at every t. Three ways out, and the choice is the build task's: solve the torsion with transverse separation at the mid-loop t as an explicit constraint; move view 4's claim to the day-28 stage where it is at least marginally true by centroid; or change the narration — but the narration is the best content in this corpus and should be the last thing that moves.

4. THE PRIMITIVE VENTRICLE FINISHES ON THE EMBRYO'S RIGHT, AND ROUND-1 ACCEPTANCE TEST B ACTIVELY ENFORCES THAT. Measured at t = 1 with the model's own axes (+x LEFT, -x RIGHT): ventricle centroid x -0.548, bulbus -0.853. Both chambers are right of the median plane. View 4 says 'The primitive ventricle moves backwards and to the left. Bulbus to the right, ventricle to the left'. The RELATIVE order is right (test F passes, the ventricle is left OF the bulbus) but the absolute side is not, and the absolute side is what is examined: the future left ventricle is left-posterior and the future right ventricle right-anterior, which is precisely why view 8's L-loop narration can say 'the morphological right ventricle on the left'. That sentence is not legible from a normal heart whose ventricles both sit on the right. THE TEST IS THE PROBLEM AS MUCH AS THE GEOMETRY: round-1 test B reads 'the loop is DEXTRAL — ventricle centroid x < 0', and the model asserts it on every build. Dextrality is a property of the bulboventricular convexity, not of the ventricle's final side, so B as written locks in the defect. Do NOT solve against B. items.standards_gap_round_3: THE STANDARD HAS A GAP AND THIS IS THE THIRD ROUND IN A ROW IT HAS COST SOMETHING. Round 2 finding 2: a test whose implementation did not match its own `must` string. Round 2 finding 4: a test that asserted a defect and so locked it in. Round 3 finding 3: a test that is CORRECT and asserts the right relation, and is satisfied by a value so small the claim is invisible — ventricle x = +0.070 on a chamber 1.329 wide passes 'ventricle centroid x > 0' at 5% of its own width. Finding 2 is the same shape: D = +0.351 passes 'atrium y - ventricle y > 0' while 97.8% of the atrium's vertical extent still overlaps the ventricle's. PROPOSED RULE, for RENDER-STANDARD and for the acceptance-test convention generally: A SIGN TEST ON A SPATIAL RELATION IS NOT A TEST. Every acceptance assertion of the form 'A is left of / above / behind B' must carry a MAGNITUDE FLOOR expressed as a fraction of the relevant extent of the structures being compared — as a starting figure, a separation of at least 35% of the mean of the two structures' extents along that axis, so that the relation is legible in the picture and not merely true in the arithmetic. Sign-only tests should be written as `> 0.35 * meanExtent`, not `> 0`, and any existing sign test should be read as UNPROVEN until it carries a floor. The deeper rule, which is what the three rounds actually demonstrate: A TEST THAT CAN BE SATISFIED WITHOUT THE PICTURE CHANGING IS NOT MEASURING WHAT THE NARRATION CLAIMS. The narration is about what a student can SEE; the tests should be too. Second, smaller gap: the review standard says 'console clean — no errors, no warnings' but nothing says a self-check must distinguish CANNOT MEASURE from MEASURED AND WRONG. Corrected here as (a); the rule is that a probe with a degenerate case must report the degeneracy, because a warning that is a known false alarm trains every future run to ignore the channel it is printed on.

POLICY IMPLEMENTED AND APPLIED 2026-09-10, by a different route than either earlier proposal. tools/apply-mesh-budget.mjs. NOT a two-tier scheme: ONE file per mesh, sized so that every scene it appears in stays under a per-scene triangle budget. This makes MESH_TIERS unnecessary — no tier map, no on-demand upgrade, no 404 fallback path, and the browser never has to know a triangle count before paying for it, which was the objection that killed the earlier proposal. BUDGET IS MEASURED, NOT CHOSEN: 450,000 tri/scene (21.5MB) = the vertebral column at full scan resolution, the heaviest scene we have evidence loads. Within an over-budget scene the share is proportional to source complexity, which recovers 'by role' from geometry without needing the role field at all — the subject of a scene is nearly always its most complex mesh. Floor 6,000 (a lumbar vertebra carries every process and facet at ~7,000; verified a rib at 6,000 against its 44,634 scan and they are indistinguishable). Never-go-backwards clamp: no mesh is ever given less than it already ships. RESULT: 254 of 494 meshes now ship at FULL SCAN RESOLUTION (was 142); corpus 2,049,168 -> 6,640,572 tri (97.7MB -> 316.6MB in the bucket); no scene exceeds 21.6MB; median scene 4MB -> ~11MB. 333 meshes re-decimated, 0 failed, worst surface deviation across the whole corpus 0.489mm, bbox bit-identical on every one so no landmark anchor moved.

note_neuro: The 13 neuroanatomy items were added 2026-09-10 once the old 'MedBank 3D scene author (v2)' task was confirmed to have stopped (last run 07:07 UTC, missed the two slots after it), so there is no second writer on this course. policy_no_mesh_means_procedural: Frank, 2026-09-10: WHERE NO MESH EXISTS, GO PROCEDURAL IMMEDIATELY — do not leave a scene planned waiting for a mesh that is not coming. Checked against the corpus before adopting: the four cerebellum/brainstem scenes held back as 'needs a mesh' carry ZERO bodyparts3d refs between them, across 35 structures. There was nothing to wait for. The judgement that still stands is RENDER-STANDARD §5 — if the form is irregular and a student is examined on recognising it EXACTLY, say so and escalate rather than shipping a plausible fake. The rule is 'no mesh means build it', not 'no mesh means pretend'.
